properties.description:
Recorded with add_epoch because it HAPPENED, on Anthony's word the same day: "Go with your suggestion for two legs and no more: skill only and lens line carries names beside ids." Sequence 493 places it after the two field-report walks (491, 492) and inside the still-planned increment epoch:planned-the-mechanism-reaches-the-moment, which it is adjacent to rather than part of — it came from his brainstorm on flo2 (one repo shared with Alex), not from a field report.

WHAT ARRIVED. req:the-agent-says-which-recorded-reader-it-assumes-and-the-lens-names-them (accepted, his signature) and cap:the-lens-names-the-person-beside-the-id-and-orientation-offers-the-match. Leg 1: ReaderLens carries names; lens_line renders "who:ajs (Anthony Sligar)" on every skill and loop_status reply, and says, when more than one background is recorded, to match the git author, offer the match in one sentence, and attribute to the same person. Leg 2: the orientation skill's reader step carries the several-readers clause in all three mirrored copies, held by a lint contract (READER_CONTRACT). Four served-reply tests and three lint checks, each observed failing first.

WHAT DID NOT ARRIVE, deliberately: the seat does not record the reader; no email or other identity signal is recorded; the persona stays per-graph. Same machine is not same person, which is why this offers and never assumes.
properties.name: ARRIVED 2026-09-14 — two legs and no more: the lens line names each person beside their id, and orientation offers the git-author match as an assumption when a design records more than one reader
